### Inspecting library sizes and removing chloroplast, mitochondria
```{r decontamination}
setwd("~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-PNNL/Documents/TES drydown experiment/qiime output files")

if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
  install.packages("BiocManager")

BiocManager::install("phyloseq")
library(phyloseq)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)
library(grid)
library(reshape2)
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
  install.packages("BiocManager")

BiocManager::install("decontam")

library(decontam)

otu = read.csv("otu_table.csv", sep=",", row.names=1)##CHANGE OTU HEADER TO OTUID IN CSV FILE 
tax = read.csv("taxonomy.csv", sep=",", row.names=1)
tax = as.matrix(tax)
metadata = read.csv("metadata-decontam.csv", sep=",", row.names=1)
OTU = otu_table(otu, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)
TAX = tax_table(tax)
meta = sample_data(metadata)

phyloseq_merged = phyloseq(OTU, TAX, meta)
phyloseq_merged

sample_names(phyloseq_merged)

##check column names of taxonomy table
colnames(tax_table(phyloseq_merged))

##remove mito, chloroplast and archaea, eukarya
phyloseq_merged_clean <- phyloseq_merged %>%
  subset_taxa(
    Domain == "d__Bacteria" &
      Family   != "f__Chloroplast" &
      Family  != "f__Mitochondria"
  )
phyloseq_merged_clean

head(sample_data(phyloseq_merged_clean))

##inspect library sizes
df <- as.data.frame(sample_data(phyloseq_merged_clean)) # Put sample_data into a ggplot-friendly data.frame
df$LibrarySize <- sample_sums(phyloseq_merged_clean)
df <- df[order(df$LibrarySize),]
df$Index <- seq(nrow(df))
plot<- ggplot(data=df, aes(x=Index, y=LibrarySize, color=Sample_type)) + geom_point() ##Supplemental Figure S3

ggsave(filename = "RMDplots/librarySize_rmd.pdf", plot = plot,
       width = 16,
       height = 13, units = c("cm"),
       dpi = 300)

```

### Decontaminant diagnostics and removal
```{r decontamination part 2}
##identify contaminants by prevalence. in this method, the distribution 
#of the frequency of each sequence feature as a function of the 
#prevalence is used to identify contaminants. In this method, 
#the prevalence (presence/absence across samples) of each sequence feature 
#in true positive samples is compared to the prevalence in negative controls 
#to identify contaminants.
setwd("~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-PNNL/Documents/TES drydown experiment/qiime output files")

sample_data(phyloseq_merged_clean)$is.neg <- sample_data(phyloseq_merged_clean)$Sample_type == "Control Sample"
contamdf.prev0.5 <- isContaminant(phyloseq_merged_clean, method="prevalence", neg="is.neg", threshold=0.5)
table(contamdf.prev0.5$contaminant)


# Make phyloseq object of presence-absence in negative controls and true samples
ps.pa <- transform_sample_counts(phyloseq_merged_clean, function(abund) 1*(abund>0))
ps.pa.neg <- prune_samples(sample_data(ps.pa)$Sample_type == "Control Sample", ps.pa)
ps.pa.pos <- prune_samples(sample_data(ps.pa)$Sample_type == "True Sample", ps.pa)
# Make data.frame of prevalence in positive and negative samples
df.pa <- data.frame(pa.pos=taxa_sums(ps.pa.pos), pa.neg=taxa_sums(ps.pa.neg),
                    contaminant=contamdf.prev0.5$contaminant)
plot<- ggplot(data=df.pa, aes(x=pa.neg, y=pa.pos, color=contaminant)) + geom_point() +
  xlab("Prevalence (Negative Controls)") + ylab("Prevalence (True Samples)") ##Supplemental Figure S3

ggsave(filename = "RMDplots/prevalence_rmd.pdf", plot = plot,
       width = 16,
       height = 13, units = c("cm"),
       dpi = 300)

write.csv(df.pa, "RMDplots/contaminant-table_rmd.csv")

write.csv(contamdf.prev0.5, "RMDplots/contaminant-prev-0.5_rmd.csv")

```

### Rarefy reads to even depth
```{r rarefy reads}
##for alpha diversity use rarefy (which already should include many subsamples and calculates alpha diversity richness and sd) or avgdist function in vegan package or use rrarefy/rarefy_even_depth and then calculate richness/diversity and repeat for 100 or 1000 times to get mean richness/diversity and std error. (https://journals.asm.org/doi/10.1128/msphere.00354-23)
##for general rarefaction of data, consider using either rarefy_even_depth with replacement (compatible with phyloseq) or the rrarefy in vegan without replacement
##rarefy will not work for diversity metrics like shannon and inverse simpson

setwd("~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-PNNL/Documents/TES drydown experiment/qiime output files")

library(vegan)

phyloseq_rarefy<- rarefy_even_depth(phyloseq_merged, sample.size = 5000, rngseed = TRUE, trimOTUs=FALSE)

sample_df <- data.frame(sample_data(phyloseq_rarefy))

write.csv(sample_df, "RMDplots/samples_rarefied_5k_rmd.csv")

##use anti-join to select non-present samples in rarefied object
#This join is like eg: for df1-df2, it selects all rows from df1 that are not present in df2.
df1<- read.csv("RMDplots/samples_pre_rarefied_rmd.csv")
df2 <- read.csv("RMDplots/samples_rarefied_5k_rmd.csv")
df= df1 %>% anti_join(df2,by="X")

write.csv(df, "RMDplots/samples-lost-rarefaction-5k_rmd.csv")

OTU2 = as(otu_table(phyloseq_rarefy), "matrix")

# Coerce to data.frame
OTUdf = as.data.frame(OTU2)

write.csv(OTUdf, "RMDplots/OTU_clean_noneg_rarefied5k_rmd.csv")

```

```{r ordination plots, out.width=c('500px','500px','500px','500px','500px','500px','500px','500px','500px'), out.height=c('400px','400px','400px','400px','400px','400px','400px','400px','400px')}
set.seed(1)
library(vegan)
#adonis(phyloseq_bray ~ saturation*time*depth, by="margin", data = sample_df)
adonis2(phyloseq_bray ~ saturation*time*depth, by="terms",data = sample_df) #gives same result as above code
##adding drying to the terms
adonis2(phyloseq_bray ~ saturation*time*depth*drying, by="terms",data = sample_df) 

packageVersion("vegan")
```

###Statistics (differences between sarturation and time for individual classes)
```{r statistics for individual classes, Kruskal Wallis and Dunn's test}

otu_final<- read.csv("OTU_Washington_rarefied5k.csv", sep=",",row.names=1)

any(rowSums(otu_final[])<1)

otu1 = otu_final[rowSums(otu_final[])<1, ,drop=FALSE] #10,456 otus with no counts, this makes total otus less for wa than before 
View(otu1)

max(rowSums(otu1))
otu_final = otu_final[rowSums(otu_final[])>0, ,drop=FALSE] ##drop taxa that are not present in any samples, 40216 taxa remains
View(otu_final)##17459 otus

library(phyloseq)


tax<- read.csv("taxonomy.csv", sep=",", row.names=1)

metadata_new<- read.csv("metadata_merge_noNA.csv", sep=",", row.names=1)

metadata_new_wa<- metadata_new %>% filter(site=="Washington")

##changing length of time to numeric value to plot by size
metadata_new_wa_edit<- metadata_new_wa %>% mutate(time=recode(length, "timezero"="Day 0",
                                                              "30d"="Day 30",
                                                              "90d"="Day 90",
                                                              "150d"="Day 150",
                                                              "1000d"="Day 1000"))
metadata_new_wa_edit$time<-factor(metadata_new_wa_edit$time, levels=c("Day 0", "Day 30" , "Day 90", "Day 150", "Day 1000"), ordered =TRUE)
metadata_new_wa_edit$saturation<- factor(metadata_new_wa_edit$saturation, levels=c("timezero", "drought", "d+rewet", ordered=TRUE))

phyloseq_wa<- sample_data(metadata_new_wa_edit)
tax = as.matrix(tax) 

otu<- otu_table(otu_final, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)
tax<- tax_table(tax)


colnames(tax)
tax
phyloseq_merged<- merge_phyloseq(otu, tax, phyloseq_wa)
phyloseq_merged

phyloseq_class <- phyloseq_merged %>%
  tax_glom(taxrank = "Class") %>%  # agglomerate at family/phylum level
  #group_by(Class, saturation, depth, site) %>% 
  transform_sample_counts(function(x) {x/sum(x)} ) %>% # Transform to rel. abundance
  psmelt() %>%                                         # Melt to long format
  #filter(Abundance > 0.01) %>%                         # Filter out low abundance taxa
  arrange(Class) # Sort data frame alphabetically by phylum/family etc

##drought
##############

phyloseq_class_drought<- phyloseq_class %>% filter(saturation=="drought")

##by time 

##Firmicutes (Bacilli)
phyloseq_class_drought_bacilli<- phyloseq_class_drought %>% filter(Class=="c__Bacilli")
kruskal.results<- kruskal.test(Abundance~length, data=phyloseq_class_drought_bacilli)
print(kruskal.results)


library(rstatix)

# Perform pairwise comparisons
posthoc_result <- phyloseq_class_drought_bacilli %>%
  dunn_test(Abundance~ length, p.adjust.method = "bonferroni")

posthoc_result
```

```{r adonis comparing drought to drought+rewet}
setwd("~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-PNNL/Documents/TES drydown experiment/qiime output files")
```

```{r alpha diversity, warning=FALSE, out.width=c('700px','700px','500px','500px','500px','500px'), out.height=c('600px','600px','400px','400px','400px','400px')}
##richness (observed OTUs) estimates, inverse simpson

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(vegan)
library(reshape2)
library(scales)
library(grid)
library(readxl)


# Initialize matrices to store richness and evenness estimates
nsamp = nsamples(phyloseq_merged)
trials = 100
richness <- matrix(nrow = nsamp, ncol = trials)
row.names(richness) <- sample_names(phyloseq_merged)
evenness <- matrix(nrow = nsamp, ncol = trials)
row.names(evenness) <- sample_names(phyloseq_merged)
# It is always important to set a seed when you subsample so your result is replicable, note of caution that this will yield different results of alpha diversity depending on the version of R being used. This is because set.seed function can vary across R versions. Here I am reporting results from R v.3.4.0 
set.seed(3)
for (i in 1:100) {
  # Subsample
  r <- rarefy_even_depth(phyloseq_merged, sample.size = 5000, verbose = FALSE, replace = TRUE) 
  
  # Calculate richness
  rich <- as.numeric(as.matrix(estimate_richness(phyloseq_merged, measures = "Observed"))) ##changed r to phyloseq_merged, no second rarefaction
  richness[ ,i] <- rich
  
  # Calculate evenness
  even <- as.numeric(as.matrix(estimate_richness(phyloseq_merged, measures = "InvSimpson"))) ##changed r to phyloseq_merged, no second rarefaction
  evenness[ ,i] <- even
}
# Create a new dataframe to hold the means and standard deviations of richness estimates
DOC_ID <- row.names(richness)
mean <- apply(richness, 1, mean)
sd <- apply(richness, 1, sd)
measure <- rep("Richness", nsamp)
rich_stats <- data.frame(DOC_ID, mean, sd, measure)
# Create a new dataframe to hold the means and standard deviations of evenness estimates
DOC_ID <- row.names(evenness)
mean <- apply(evenness, 1, mean)
sd <- apply(evenness, 1, sd) 
measure <- rep("Inverse Simpson", nsamp)
even_stats <- data.frame(DOC_ID, mean, sd, measure)
alpha <- rbind(rich_stats, even_stats)

s <- read.csv("metadata_merge_noNA.csv")
alphadiv <- merge(alpha, s, by = "DOC_ID") 
write.csv(alphadiv,file = "RMDplots/alphadiv_ak_wa_rmd.csv")

dim(alphadiv_ak)

write.csv(alphadiv_wa, file="RMDplots/alphadiv_wa_rmd.csv")

  geom_text(data=summarized, aes(x=summarized$length, y =2500,

            check_overlap = T,

         axis.title.x= element_text(size=16, color="black"),

         panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "black"), 
         legend.title = element_text(size =14, colour = "black"),
         legend.text = element_text(size = 12, colour = "black")) +
  guides(linetype = guide_legend(override.aes= list(color = "black")), color= guide_legend(order = 1)) +
  xlab("Time") +labs(color="saturation")
```

```{r indicator species test}
setwd("~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-PNNL/Documents/TES drydown experiment/qiime output files")

otu_final = read.csv("OTU_clean_noneg_rarefied5k.csv", sep=",", row.names=1) ##USING UNRAREFIED DATA, CAN ALSO CHECK WITH RAREFIED 

otu_final = otu_final[rowSums(otu_final[])>0, ,drop=FALSE] ##drop taxa that are not present in any samples, 40216 taxa remains

tax = read.csv("taxonomy.csv", sep=",", row.names=1)
tax = as.matrix(tax)

metadata = read.csv("metadata_merge_noNA.csv", sep=",", row.names=1) # use for crop indicators

phyloseq_merged

##indicator species analysis

library(indicspecies)

GetIndicators <-function(dataframe, var){
  require(phyloseq); require(indicspecies); require(dplyr)
  #dataframe <- tax_glom(dataframe, taxrank = "Family") ##can be adjusted to indicate at family or class level, else default is OTU level
  otu <- as.data.frame(otu_table(dataframe, taxa_are_rows = TRUE))
  metadata = as(sample_data(dataframe), "data.frame")
  taxa <- as.data.frame(as.matrix(tax_table(dataframe)))
  multipatt <- multipatt(t(otu), metadata[,var], func = "r.g",
                         control=how(nperm=999), duleg=FALSE)
  multipatt -> multipatt_fdr
  multipatt_fdr$sign$p.value <- p.adjust(multipatt_fdr$sign$p.value, "fdr")
  #print(multipatt_fdr)
  multipatt_fdr$sign[which(
    multipatt_fdr$sign$p.value <= 0.05), ] -> indicator_taxa
  taxa$OTU <- rownames(taxa)
  data.frame(OTU = as.factor(row.names(indicator_taxa)), indicator_taxa) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(taxa, by="OTU") -> indicator_taxa
  rownames(indicator_taxa) <- indicator_taxa$OTU
  indicator_taxa <- arrange(indicator_taxa, desc(stat))
  return(indicator_taxa)
}

  GetIndicators(dataframe=phyloseq_merged, "site")

write.csv(ind_region, "RMDplots/indicator_site_ak_wa_rmd.csv")
```

```{r heatmap of abundance (48 unique indicator species at 1000 day drought), fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
setwd("~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-PNNL/Documents/TES drydown experiment/qiime output files")

otu_wa<- read.csv("RMDplots/OTU_Washington_rarefied5k_rmd.csv", row.names=1)
otu_wa_new <- cbind(OTU = rownames(otu_wa), otu_wa)
ind_length_wa<-read.csv("ind_length_wa_drought_timezero_genus.csv", row.names=1)
##subsetting to the 48 unique indicators for drought 1000d
ind_length_wa<- ind_length_wa %>% filter(s.1000d==1 & s.30d==0 & s.90d==0, s.timezero==0) #use when plotting only the 48 taxa

##join otu table with indicator taxa
ind_wa_abund<- left_join(ind_length_wa, otu_wa_new, by="OTU") ##using the drought +time zero ind by length at genus level

rownames(ind_wa_abund) <- ind_wa_abund[,1]
ind_wa_mat = ind_wa_abund[,17:ncol(ind_wa_abund)] ##change the column number as appropriate, changed from 16


##changing the ind_wa_mat data frame to new_df_drought_wide
##because we dont need to filter any samples as below
new_df_drought_wide<- ind_wa_mat

##drought samples WA with time zero, or drought plus time zero and d+rewet
ind_wa_50 <- new_df_drought_wide[order(rowSums(new_df_drought_wide), decreasing = TRUE),]
#ind_wa_50 <- ind_wa_50[c(1:50),] ##select top 50 most abundant Classes, skip this step when working with 48 taxa


mat_data<- ind_wa_50 

#REMOVE OTUS that cant be plotted in heatmap, note which ones are removed, if there are only numbers nothing is removed. if there are NAs some may be removed.

sum(is.na(as.matrix(dist(mat_data))))

giveNAs = which(is.na(as.matrix(dist(mat_data))),arr.ind=TRUE)
head(giveNAs)

tab = sort(table(c(giveNAs)),decreasing=TRUE)
checkNA = sapply(1:length(tab),function(i){
  sum(is.na(as.matrix(dist(mat_data[-as.numeric(names(tab[1:i])),]))))
})
rmv = names(tab)[1:min(which(checkNA==0))] ##https://stackoverflow.com/questions/61469201/pheatmap-won-t-cluster-rows-na-nan-inf-in-foreign-function-call-arg-10 
rmv ## the intention with this code is not to remove rows but to see for which ASVs are we not able to calculate a distance for the heatmap

##use this line only if something needs to be removed
#mat_data = mat_data[-as.numeric(rmv),] 
#View(mat_data)


####merge taxonomy with OTU hash id

taxonomy<- read.csv("taxonomy.csv", row.names=1)
taxonomy_family<- taxonomy %>% dplyr::select(c("Family", "Class"))

mat_data_merge <- merge(mat_data, taxonomy_family, by="row.names")

mat_data_merge$OTUclass <- paste(mat_data_merge$Class, mat_data_merge$Row.names)

rnames <-mat_data_merge$OTUclass
rownames(mat_data_merge) <- rnames  # assign row names

mat_data_merge_otuclass<- mat_data_merge %>% dplyr::select(!Row.names)%>% dplyr::select (!Family) %>% dplyr::select(!Class) %>% dplyr::select(!OTUclass)


library(pheatmap)
library(vegan)

#mat_data_merge_otuclass<-read.csv("mat_data_merge_otuclass_wa_drought_timezero_drewet_rarefied5k.csv", row.names=1, check.names=FALSE)#for drought times heatmap with d+rewet (with time zero)
mat_data_merge_otuclass<-read.csv("mat_data_merge_otuclass_wa_drought_timezero_drewet_rarefied5k_48unique1000d.csv", row.names=1, check.names=FALSE) # drought times heatmap with d+rewet (with time zero, only the 48 unique taxa at 1000d)

mat_data_merge_otuclass<- as.data.frame(mat_data_merge_otuclass)
class(mat_data_merge_otuclass)

##replace NAs with zero, not needed there should be no NAs here
matrix<- as.matrix(mat_data_merge_otuclass)
matrix[is.na(matrix)] <-0


##compute max standardization

matrix_max_standardize_wa <-decostand(matrix, method = "max", MARGIN = 1)

library(viridis)

#create the breaks

bk2 = unique(c(0.00000000, seq(0.00000001, 1.00000000, length=20)))
col1 = colorRampPalette(c("gray"))(1)
col2 =viridis(20)

colors2 <- c(col1, col2)

library(pheatmap)

##setting labels for drought samples with timezero and d+rewet
metadata_new<- read.csv("wa_rarefied_metadata.csv")
metadata_new<- metadata_new %>% filter(saturation=="drought"|saturation=="timezero"|saturation=="d+rewet")
sat_labels<-  metadata_new %>% dplyr::select("Key", "length","saturation")
sat_labels$length_new <- dplyr::recode(sat_labels$length, 
                                "30d"="day_30",
                                "90d"="day_90",
                                "1000d"="day_1000",
                                "timezero"="timezero")
row.names(sat_labels)<- metadata_new$Key
sat_labels<- sat_labels %>% dplyr::select(!c(length, Key))
sat_labels$length_new<- factor(sat_labels$length_new,levels = c("timezero", "day_30", "day_90", "day_1000"), ordered=TRUE)
sat_labels$saturation<- dplyr::recode(sat_labels$saturation,
                                      "timezero"="timezero",
                                    "drought"="drought",
                                    "d+rewet"="d_rewet")

sat_labels$saturation<- factor(sat_labels$saturation, levels= c("timezero", "drought", "d_rewet"), ordered=TRUE)
sat_labels1<- sat_labels %>% mutate(final_labels=paste(saturation,length_new)) %>% filter(!is.na(length_new))
sat_labels1$labels_true<- dplyr::recode(sat_labels1$final_labels, 
                                    "timezero timezero"="timezero",
                                    "d_rewet day_30"="d_rewet_day30",
                                    "d_rewet day_90"="d_rewet_day90",
                                    "d_rewet day_1000"="d_rewet_day1000",
                                    "drought day_30"="drought_day30",
                                    "drought day_90"="drought_day90",
                                    "drought day_1000"="drought_day1000")


#heatmap color coding by time zero, drought, drought+rewet
anno_colori <- list(labels_true=c(timezero="#CC79A7", drought_day30='#CCBB44', drought_day90='#66CCEE', drought_day1000='#EE6677',
                                 d_rewet_day30="#D55E00", d_rewet_day90="#56B4E9",d_rewet_day1000='#AA3377'))

##since the DOC sample ids are in sequence, i can directly overlay the labels 
plot_heatmap_wa <- pheatmap::pheatmap(matrix_max_standardize_wa, ##if plotting sample by sample and not the means then use matrix_max_standardize_sw
                                      annotation_col = sat_labels,
                                      annotation_colors = anno_colori,
                                      cluster_cols = F, na_col = "white", 
                                      main="Washington",
                                      #labels_row=TRUE,
                                      show_colnames = TRUE,
                                      annotation_legend = TRUE,
                                      color = colors2,
                                      breaks = bk2,
                                      clustering_distance_rows="euclidean",clustering_method = "complete"
                                     
                                      
                                      
)
##heatmap drought, drought+rewet amd time zero

##trying to order samples by length_new and saturation column
# Assuming 'length_new' is a column in 'sat_labels' for ordering
order_variables<- c("length_new", "saturation")
#Determine order according to VariableName in sat_labels
sample_order <- with(sat_labels, order(sat_labels[[order_variables[1]]], sat_labels[[order_variables[2]]]))
# Reorder the matrix's columns based on this order
ordered_matrix <- matrix_max_standardize_wa[, sample_order]
ordered_matrix<- ordered_matrix[,1:94] #removing the last couple of samples in the matrix to remove the d+rewet samples from day 150 which have no matching drought samples for that timepoint
# Reorder annotations accordingly
ordered_annotations <- sat_labels[sample_order, ]

anno_colori <- list(length_new=c(timezero="#CC79A7", day_30='#EEDD88', day_90='#BBCC33', day_1000='#AAAA00'), saturation=c(timezero="#CC79A7",drought="#E69F00", d_rewet="#0072B2"))   


plot_heatmap_wa <- pheatmap::pheatmap(ordered_matrix, ##if plotting sample by sample and not the means then use matrix_max_standardize_sw
                                      annotation_col = ordered_annotations,
                                      annotation_colors = anno_colori,
                                      cluster_cols = F, na_col = "white", 
                                      main="Washington",
                                      #labels_row=TRUE,
                                      show_colnames = TRUE,
                                      annotation_legend = TRUE,
                                      color = colors2,
                                      breaks = bk2,
                                      cluster_rows=T
                                      #clustering_distance_rows="euclidean",clustering_method = "complete"
)

ggsave(filename = "RMDplots/wa_indicator_drought_1000d_withrewet_inorder_groupedtaxa_rmd.tiff", plot = plot_heatmap_wa,
       width = 35,
       height = 20, units = c("cm"),
       dpi = 300)

      # width = 35,

     #  dpi = 300)
```

### Bray-Curtis dissimilarity heatmaps 
```{r bray curtis heatmap, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}

setwd("~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-PNNL/Documents/TES drydown experiment/qiime output files")

library(phyloseq)
library(tidyverse)
otu = read.csv("RMDplots/OTU_Washington_rarefied5k_rmd.csv", sep=",", row.names=1) ##USING RAREFIED DATA here unlike unrarefied data used for site specific indicators  

otu_final = otu[rowSums(otu[])>0, ,drop=FALSE] ##drop taxa that are not present in any samples
tax = read.csv("taxonomy.csv", sep=",", row.names=1)
tax = as.matrix(tax)

metadata = read.csv("metadata_merge_noNA.csv", sep=",", row.names=1) 

##filtering to 0-5 cm samples
metadata_wa<- metadata %>% filter(site=="Washington" & length!="150d" & depth=="0-5cm")
metadata_wa$treat_time <- paste(metadata_wa$saturation, metadata_wa$length)

OTU = otu_table(otu_final, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)
TAX = tax_table(tax)
meta = sample_data(metadata_wa)
##merge
phyloseq_merged = phyloseq(OTU, TAX, meta)
phyloseq_merged

##bray curtis distances 
otu_wa = as(otu_table(phyloseq_merged), "matrix")

# Coerce to data.frame
otu_df = as.data.frame(otu_wa)
otu_df_final = otu_df[rowSums(otu_df[])>0, ,drop=FALSE] #16041 taxa remain after filtering out 150d, 10871 taxa remain after filtering out 150d and 5cm-end samples, 9796 taxa remain after filtering out 150d and 0-5cm samples
OTU = otu_table(otu_df_final, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)

phyloseq_merged = phyloseq(OTU, TAX, meta)
bray_dist <- vegdist(t(otu_table(phyloseq_merged)), method = "bray")

bray_matrix <- as.matrix(bray_dist)

annotation_data <- data.frame(Treatment = sample_data(phyloseq_merged)$treat_time)
sample_data(phyloseq_merged)
rownames(annotation_data) <- sample_names(phyloseq_merged)
annotation_data
annotation_data$Treatment<- dplyr::recode(annotation_data$Treatment, "d+rewet 1000d"="d_rewet_1000d",
                                          "d+rewet 30d"="d_rewet_30d",
                                          "d+rewet 90d"="d_rewet_90d",
                                          "drought 30d"="drought_30d",
                                          "drought 90d"="drought_90d",
                                         "drought 1000d"="drought_1000d",
                                   "timezero timezero"="timezero")
annotation_data$Treatment<- factor(annotation_data$Treatment,levels = c("timezero", "drought_30d", "d_rewet_30d","drought_90d", "d_rewet_90d", "drought_1000d", "d_rewet_1000d"), ordered=TRUE)
annotation_data<- annotation_data %>% mutate(Treatment2 = Treatment)
annotation_data$Treatment2<- factor(annotation_data$Treatment2,levels = c("timezero", "drought_30d", "d_rewet_30d","drought_90d", "d_rewet_90d", "drought_1000d", "d_rewet_1000d"), ordered=TRUE)


annotation_colors <- list(Treatment=c(timezero="#CC79A7", drought_30d='#CCBB44', drought_90d='#66CCEE', drought_1000d='#EE6677',
                                 d_rewet_30d="#D55E00", d_rewet_90d="#56B4E9",d_rewet_1000d='#AA3377'
                                      ))

library(viridis)
#create the breaks

bk2 = unique(c(0.00000000, seq(0.00000001, 1.00000000, length=20)))
col1 = colorRampPalette(c("gray"))(1)
col2 =viridis(20)

colors2 <- c(col1, col2)

library(pheatmap)
##trying to order samples by Treatment column in annotation data
# Assuming 'Treatment' is a column in 'annotation_data' for ordering
order_variables<- c("Treatment", "Treatment2")
#Determine order according to VariableName in sat_labels
sample_order <- with(annotation_data, order(annotation_data[[order_variables[1]]], annotation_data[[order_variables[2]]]))
# Reorder the matrix's columns based on this order
ordered_matrix <- bray_matrix[sample_order, sample_order]
#ordered_matrix<- ordered_matrix[,1:94] #removing the last couple of samples in the matrix to remove the d+rewet samples from day 150 which have no matching drought samples for that timepoint
# Reorder annotations accordingly
ordered_annotations <- annotation_data[sample_order, ]

heatmap_wa_0_5<- pheatmap::pheatmap(ordered_matrix,
```

```{r dendrograms, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
  mutate(type_indicator = ifelse(
    s.1000d == 1 & s.30d == 0 & s.90d == 0 & s.timezero == 0, "drought_1000day_ind",
    ifelse(s.30d == 1 & s.90d == 0 & s.1000d == 0 & s.timezero == 0, "drought_30day_ind",
           ifelse(s.90d == 1 & s.30d == 0 & s.1000d == 0 & s.timezero == 0, "drought_90day_ind",
                  ifelse(s.30d == 1 & s.90d == 1 & s.1000d == 1 & s.timezero == 0, "drought_30day_90day_1000day_ind",
                         ifelse(s.30d == 1 & s.90d == 1 & s.1000d == 0 & s.timezero == 1, "drought_timezero_30day_90day_ind",
                                ifelse(s.30d == 1 & s.90d == 1 & s.1000d == 0 & s.timezero == 0, "drought_30day_90day_ind", 
                                       ifelse(s.30d == 0 & s.90d == 0 & s.1000d == 0 & s.timezero == 1, "timezero_ind", NA))))))))
```

### Differential expression analysis
```{r DeSeq2 for differential expression analysis, fig.width=16, fig.height=10}
setwd("~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-PNNL/Documents/TES drydown experiment/qiime output files")

##Not rarefying the data, suing raw counts for WA differentially enriched taxa by drought day
##30d versus 90d
##30d versus 1000d
##90d versus 1000d

library(DESeq2)
#options(digits=15)
#set.seed(123)
packageVersion("DESeq2") # v‘1.48.2’

##### Washington drought DeSeq analysis by time 
otu_final = read.csv("OTU_clean.csv", sep=",", row.names=1)##CHANGE OTU HEADER TO OTUID IN CSV FILE 

any(rowSums(otu_final[])<1)

otu1 = otu_final[rowSums(otu_final[])<1, ,drop=FALSE] #10303 otus with no counts for 7k rarefied table, 12697 otus with no count for 5k rarefied table
max(rowSums(otu1))
otu_final = otu_final[rowSums(otu_final[])>0, ,drop=FALSE] ##drop taxa that are not present in any samples, 30309 taxa remains for 7k, 27915 taxa remains for 5k

library(phyloseq)

tax<- read.csv("taxonomy.csv", sep=",", row.names=1)
metadata <- read.csv("metadata_merge_noNA.csv", sep=",", row.names=1)

tax = as.matrix(tax) 

otu<- otu_table(otu_final, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)
tax<- tax_table(tax)
metadata<- sample_data(metadata)

colnames(tax)
phyloseq_merged<- merge_phyloseq(otu, tax, metadata)
phyloseq_merged

###30 days, 1000 days
metadata_new <- read.csv("metadata_merge_noNA.csv", sep=",", row.names=1)
library(tidyverse)
metadata_new <- metadata_new %>% filter(site=="Washington", length==c("30d","1000d"))
keep.samples <- as.vector(metadata_new$Key)
keep.samples

phyloseq_merged_final <- prune_samples(keep.samples, phyloseq_merged) 
phyloseq_merged_final
# Assuming 'physeq_obj' is your phyloseq object after prune_samples()
# 1. Get the sum of counts for each taxon
taxa_sums_after_prune <- taxa_sums(phyloseq_merged_final)

# 2. Identify taxa that have a sum greater than 0 (i.e., are still present)
present_taxa <- names(taxa_sums_after_prune[taxa_sums_after_prune > 0])

# 3. Prune the phyloseq object to keep only the present taxa
##30 day , 1000d 
phyloseq_merged_filtered_30_1000 <- prune_taxa(present_taxa, phyloseq_merged_final)
phyloseq_merged_filtered_30_1000

head(sample_data(phyloseq_merged_filtered_30_1000)$length, 24)

##convert phyloseq format to DESEq dataset with dispersions estimated using the experimental design formula
diagdds = phyloseq_to_deseq2(phyloseq_merged_filtered_30_1000, ~ length)
diagdds$length
diagdds

diagdds$length <-factor(diagdds$length, levels = c("30d", "1000d"))
diagdds$length #make sure that Control is the first level in the treatment factor, so that the default log2 fold changes are calculated as treatment over control and not the other way around.

cts <- counts(diagdds)
geoMeans <- apply(cts, 1, function(row) if (all(row == 0)) 0 else exp(mean(log(row[row != 0]))))
diagdds <- estimateSizeFactors(diagdds, geoMeans=geoMeans)
diagdds = DESeq(diagdds, test="Wald", fitType="parametric")
diagdds

##The default multiple-inference correction is Benjamini-Hochberg, and occurs within the DESeq function.

#The following results function call creates a table of the results of the tests. Very fast. 
#The hard work was already stored with the rest of the DESeq2-related data in our latest version 
#of the diagdds object (see above). I then order by the adjusted p-value, removing the entries 
#with an NA value. The rest of this example is just formatting the results table with taxonomic information for nice(ish) display.


res = results(diagdds, cooksCutoff = FALSE)
alpha = 0.01
table(is.na(res$padj))
summary(res$padj < alpha)

sigtab = res[which(res$padj < alpha), ]
sigtab = cbind(as(sigtab, "data.frame"), as(tax_table(phyloseq_merged_filtered_30_1000)[rownames(sigtab), ], "matrix"))
head(sigtab)
dim(sigtab)


#The following makes a nice ggplot2 summary of the results.

library(ggplot2)
library(viridis)

theme_set(theme_bw())
# Phylum order
x = tapply(sigtab$log2FoldChange, sigtab$Phylum, function(x) max(x))
x = sort(x, TRUE)
sigtab$Phylum = factor(as.character(sigtab$Phylum), levels=names(x))
# Genus order
x = tapply(sigtab$log2FoldChange, sigtab$Genus, function(x) max(x))
x = sort(x, TRUE)
sigtab$Genus = factor(as.character(sigtab$Genus), levels=names(x))


##The DESeq2 function is outputting a different result in markdown than what is coming out in console for the R studio 2025 version, the console version is correct
##However, the console version from R studio 2025 also differs from the results generated in R studio 2023 version, though both are correct with minor differences in taxonomic representation

write.csv(sigtab, "RMDplots/sigtab_30d_1000d_WA_enriched_depleted_in1000d_rmd.csv")
```

```{r BC similarity to Day 0}
######ANCOVA
#Outliers
#An outlier is a point that has an extreme outcome variable value. The presence of outliers may affect the interpretation of the 
#model.

#Outliers can be identified by examining the standardized residual (or studentized residual), which is the residual divided by its estimated standard error. Standardized residuals can be interpreted as the number of standard errors away from the regression line.

#Observations whose standardized residuals are greater than 3 in absolute value are possible outliers.
###normality of residuals
# Fit the model, the covariate goes first
model <- lm(distance ~ time + saturation_y, data = BC_time)
# Inspect the model diagnostic metrics
model.metrics <- augment(model) %>%
  select(-.hat, -.sigma, -.fitted) # Remove details
head(model.metrics, 3)
model.metrics %>% 
  filter(abs(.std.resid) > 3) %>%
  as.data.frame()

###homogeneity of regression slopes
##This assumption checks that there is no significant interaction between the covariate and the grouping variable. This can be evaluated as follows:

##without outliers
BC_time_no_outliers %>% anova_test(distance ~ saturation_y*time, covariate = time, type=3) 


##A significant interaction implies that the relationship between the covariate and dependent variable is different across groups

###normality of residuals
# Fit the model, the covariate goes first
model <- lm(distance ~ time + saturation_y, data = BC_time_no_outliers)
# Inspect the model diagnostic metrics
model.metrics <- augment(model) %>%
  select(-.hat, -.sigma, -.fitted) # Remove details
head(model.metrics, 3)


# Assess normality of residuals using shapiro wilk test, data not normal if p is less than 0.05, then test is significant

shapiro_test(model.metrics$.resid)

##after removing outliers the statistic improved and the p value increased so keeping this



#Homogeneity of variances
#ANCOVA assumes that the variance of the residuals is equal for all groups. This can be checked using the Levene’s test:
  
model.metrics %>% levene_test(.resid ~ saturation_y)

#if Levene’s test is significant (p < 0.05), so we cannot assume homogeneity of the residual variances for all groups.
##after removing outliers the p value increased so keeping this






#Computation
#The orders of variables matters when computing ANCOVA. You want to remove the effect of the covariate first - that is, you want to control for it - prior to entering your main variable or interest.

#The covariate goes first (there is interaction)! If you do not do this in order, you will get different results.
res.aov <- BC_time_no_outliers %>% anova_test(distance ~ time + saturation_y, type=3)
get_anova_table(res.aov)

#After adjustment for time (covariate), there was a statistically significant difference in bray curtis distance between the groups, F(1, 357) = 394.912, p < 0.0001.



#Post-hoc test
#Pairwise comparisons can be performed to identify which groups are different. The Bonferroni multiple testing correction is applied. 
#This can be easily done using the function emmeans_test() [rstatix package], a wrapper around the emmeans package, which needs to be installed. 
#Emmeans stands for estimated marginal means (aka least square means or adjusted means).

# Pairwise comparisons
library(emmeans)
pwc <- BC_time_no_outliers %>% 
  emmeans_test(
    distance ~ saturation_y, covariate = time,
    p.adjust.method = "bonferroni"
  )
pwc

##without outliers
    

# Display the adjusted means of each group
# Also called as the estimated marginal means (emmeans)
get_emmeans(pwc)

#Data are adjusted mean +/- standard error. The means distance was statistically significantly greater in d+rewet compared to drought, p < 0.001.
##after removing outliers



# Visualization: line plots with p-values
pwc <- pwc %>% add_xy_position(x = "saturation_y", fun = "mean_se")
ancova_corrected_for_time<- ggline(get_emmeans(pwc), x = "saturation_y", y = "emmean") +
  geom_point(aes(x=saturation_y, y=emmean), size=5, color=c("#E69F00", "#0072B2"))+
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), width = 0.2) + 
  stat_pvalue_manual(pwc, hide.ns = TRUE, tip.length = FALSE) +
  labs(
    subtitle = get_test_label(res.aov, detailed = TRUE),
    caption = get_pwc_label(pwc)
  )

ancova_corrected_for_time

ggsave(filename = "RMDplots/ancova_no_outliers.tiff", plot = ancova_corrected_for_time,
       width = 20,
       height = 15, units = c("cm"),
       dpi = 300)
```
